failures.title: Ford YLFS Engine Problems - What Actually Fails

items.title: Wet Timing Belt Degradation - 2016-2019 models primarily
items.whatHappens: The YLFS 2.0 EcoBlue utilises a wet timing belt design that runs submerged in engine oil. Early production units (2016-2019) are particularly susceptible to belt material degradation, where the rubber sheds microscopic debris into the lubrication system. This debris travels through the oil galleries and clogs the oil pickup strainer, leading to a sudden drop in oil pressure. If ignored, this causes catastrophic oil starvation, resulting in spun bearings, scored cylinder walls, and total Ford YLFS engine failure.
items.repairVsReplace: If caught early during routine servicing, a preventative wet belt replacement (£600-£1,200) is sufficient. However, once oil starvation symptoms (like a rattling noise or oil pressure warning light) appear, a full Ford YLFS engine replacement (£2,000-£4,500 fitted) is almost always required. Read our full timing belt failure guide for early warning signs.

items.title: DPF Clogging & EGR Issues - Urban/commercial use primarily
items.whatHappens: As a modern diesel designed for emissions compliance, the YLFS is equipped with a diesel particulate filter (DPF) and exhaust gas recirculation (EGR) system. Vehicles used primarily for short urban trips or stop-start commercial duties (particularly Transit Custom vans) suffer from incomplete DPF regeneration cycles. This leads to DPF clogging, increased exhaust backpressure, and strain on the turbocharger. The EGR valve is also prone to carbon buildup, causing rough running and fault codes.
items.repairVsReplace: A clogged DPF can sometimes be forced to regenerate or chemically cleaned (£400-£1,200). If the DPF has failed completely, replacement is required (£800-£1,800). EGR valve cleaning or replacement ranges from £300-£900. If the turbocharger has been damaged by excessive backpressure, turbo replacement adds £800-£2,000. Read our full DPF clogging guide for prevention advice.

failures.goodYearsLine: Post-2019 revisions of the YLFS received updated wet belt materials and tensioners that significantly reduce the degradation risk. However, strict adherence to the 6- to 8-year replacement interval and the use of correct Ford-spec oil remains critical to avoid this failure pattern .

variants.title: How to Confirm You Have the Ford YLFS
variants.intro: The YLFS engine code is physically stamped on a machined pad on the engine block, typically located near the dipstick tube or where the block meets the gearbox bellhousing. It is also clearly listed on your vehicle's V5C registration document under the engine code section. The YLFS is most commonly confused with the older 2.0 TDCi engines (such as the UFDA or QXDA codes) which share similar displacement but use a completely different fuel system architecture and ECU calibration. Fitting a 2.0 TDCi into a YLFS-configured vehicle without extensive ECU remapping, loom adaptation, and fuel system changes will cause severe running issues, fault codes, and potential limp-mode activation. The 2.0 EcoBlue also features a different turbo setup, emissions equipment, and wet belt timing system that the older TDCi lacks. Always verify the exact YLFS code before authorising a swap.

buyingGuide.title: Buying a Replacement Ford YLFS - What to Choose

options.label: Used
options.body: A used Ford YLFS engine makes sense only if you have absolute documented proof that the wet timing belt was replaced within the last 20,000 miles and the oil system is free of contamination. The primary risk with a used 2.0 EcoBlue is inheriting an engine with degraded belt material in the sump or pre-existing oil starvation damage. Explore vetted options via our used engines network.

options.label: Reconditioned
options.body: This is the strongly recommended choice for most Ford YLFS owners. A proper reconditioned Ford YLFS engine will include a brand-new wet timing belt kit, updated tensioners, a thoroughly cleaned oil gallery, and a checked turbocharger. This directly addresses the dominant failure mode, providing a reliable, long-term solution without the premium cost of a full strip-and-rebuild. View reconditioned engines for detailed specifications.

options.label: Rebuilt
options.body: A full rebuild is justified if the cylinder walls were scored during an oil starvation event, or if the turbocharger disintegrated and sent debris into the intake. A comprehensive rebuilt Ford YLFS engine should include new pistons and rings, a machined or replaced block, and all-new sealing components alongside the mandatory wet belt service. Learn more about rebuilt engines.

buyingGuide.supplyFitLine: Fitting a Ford YLFS through our network ensures the work is completed by specialists familiar with EcoBlue fuel system and timing procedures, backed by a minimum 12-month warranty and nationwide delivery. Arrange supply and fit for complete peace of mind.
buyingGuide.vehicleValueNote: Ford Transit Custom and Kuga 2.0 EcoBlue host vehicles (2016+) typically hold a current UK market value of £8,000-£25,000 . With a reconditioned Ford YLFS replacement costing £1,890-£3,320 fully fitted, the total repair is generally viable for most examples. However, for older Transit Custom vans with high mileage or commercial wear, replacement costs may approach 40-60% of vehicle value. If the lowest viable replacement cost exceeds approximately 60% of the vehicle's current market value, evaluate scrap value before committing.

items.question: How much does a Ford YLFS engine replacement cost in the UK?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford YLFS engine costs between £1,500 and £2,800 for supply only, or £1,890 to £3,320 fully fitted by an independent specialist. Used units start around £500 but carry a high risk of inherited wet belt degradation. Rebuilt units range from £2,500 to £4,000, addressing any cylinder scoring from prior oil starvation.

items.question: What is the most common failure with the Ford YLFS engine?
items.answer: The dominant failure is wet timing belt degradation, typically occurring between 60,000 and 100,000 miles. The belt runs in the engine oil and can shed rubber debris, especially in early 2016-2019 production units. This debris clogs the oil pickup strainer, leading to catastrophic oil starvation and total engine failure.

items.question: Should I buy a used or reconditioned Ford YLFS engine?
items.answer: A reconditioned Ford YLFS is strongly recommended over a used unit due to the inherent wet belt failure risk. A proper reconditioned unit will include a brand-new wet timing belt kit, updated tensioners, and a thoroughly cleaned oil gallery. A used engine may already have degraded belt material in the sump or pre-existing oil starvation damage.
